clue.text: Still about to admit value in being bold

indicators.note: to admit something is to let it in, so one piece goes inside the other
about here means turned round, so the word for still is read backwards

parts.note: still, as in 'still here', means yet
merit is worth or value

explanation.surface: A nervous person is told they still need to see the worth in acting boldly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adjective meaning motionless, but it is the adverb, as in 'still waiting'.
explanation.definitionFit: Temerity is reckless boldness, so having it is a matter of being bold, used here as a noun phrase.

clue.text: Manage to discover about new state of mind

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to trace something is to manage to find it

explanation.surface: Someone manages to find out about a new frame of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts N inside TRACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A trance is a dazed or hypnotic mental condition, i.e. a state of mind.

clue.text: I'm very seedy, chaps, but look in

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: men are chaps
lo is an old word for look, as in 'lo and behold'

explanation.surface: Someone feeling rough tells friends to drop in anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm very seedy' sounds like being unwell, but it is the fruit speaking, and 'lo' is an archaic word for look.
explanation.definitionFit: A melon is a fruit packed with seeds, so it could describe itself as very seedy.

clue.text: Philosopher in group of universities

explanation.surface: A thinker belongs to a group of universities.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertrand Russell was a British philosopher; the Russell Group is a club of leading UK research universities.

clue.text: Reverse fortune, as spiritualists used to?

explanation.surface: Spiritualists once reversed their luck.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn the tables is to reverse one's position; Victorian spiritualists held table-turning seances.

clue.text: Fail to take advantage of col?

explanation.surface: A mountaineer turns down the chance to cross a high pass.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the phrase literally: a col is a pass, and a pass in the mountains is up high.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass up an opportunity is to let it go by; a col is a mountain pass, which goes up.

clue.text: Novel of middle-class life written in rhyme

definitions.text: Novel of middle-class life written in rhyme

parts.words: Novel of middle-class life written in rhyme
parts.note: a genre of novel about comfortable English country households, named after a kitchen stove plus a word for a long story, the two halves rhyming

explanation.surface: A novel about bourgeois life appears to be composed in verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written in rhyme' sounds like verse, but it means the name of the genre rhymes with itself. An Aga is a cast-iron range cooker, a symbol of the British middle class.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a genre of novel set among comfortable middle-class English families with Aga cookers.

clue.text: Talent way over the top not displayed by Humpty-Dumpty

indicators.note: in a down clue, over the top means the first piece is placed above the second

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
ability is talent

explanation.surface: Excessive skill is something the nursery-rhyme egg never showed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over the top' looks like 'excessive' but places ST above ABILITY. Humpty Dumpty, the egg of the nursery rhyme, sat on a wall and had a great fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Humpty Dumpty fell off his wall, so steadiness was the quality he plainly did not show.

clue.text: Titled hero, an aristocrat not a gay book

parts.note: a peer is a member of the nobility

indicators.note: not means without, so the named letter is removed

parts.note: NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A hero with a title is an aristocrat, not a gay book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a' removes A from GAY, leaving GY. Peer Gynt is the hero of Ibsen's play, whose title is his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Peer Gynt is the hero of Ibsen's play of that title, so he is a hero who gives the play its name.

clue.text: A little drink held in case where Thomas's train halted

indicators.note: held means gripped round, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: a drop is a small amount of drink
lest means in case, as in 'lest we forget'

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a small nip of something in a case for emergencies.
explanation.walkthrough: Adlestrop is the station in Edward Thomas's famous poem where his express train stopped unexpectedly.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Thomas's poem Adlestrop recalls the train drawing up at that Gloucestershire village station.

clue.text: Sort of architecture in which all angles are right?

definitions.text: Sort of architecture in which all angles are right?

parts.words: Sort of architecture in which all angles are right?
parts.note: the name of an English Gothic style also describes lines meeting at ninety degrees

explanation.surface: A building style is described where every corner is just so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' reads as correct, but means right angles: the late English Gothic style shares its name with the word for meeting at ninety degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: Perpendicular is the late Gothic English style, and the word also means at right angles.

clue.text: Saying old-fashioned goodness needs a backing

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the exclamation is read in reverse

parts.note: egad is a dated exclamation like 'goodness!'

explanation.surface: A traditional proverb about virtue calls for some support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egad' is a dated mild oath, a softened 'by God', used much like 'goodness!'.
explanation.definitionFit: An adage is a traditional proverb or saw, i.e. a saying.

clue.text: Fancy Tory constituency? I'll say

indicators.note: I'll say signals that the words are to be spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a Conservative (Tory) constituency is a 'Con seat' in election shorthand

explanation.surface: Someone imagines a safe Conservative seat and emphatically agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Con' is the usual British shorthand for the Conservative Party, and a constituency is a parliamentary seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A conceit is a fanciful notion or elaborate figure of speech, so it is a fancy as a noun.

clue.text: Making another copy for gathering

explanation.surface: A farmhand repeats the work of collecting the harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape is to copy, so re-aping is copying again; reaping is gathering in a crop.

clue.text: Harmonic clash is, after all, one possibility

indicators.note: possibility suggests one of several arrangements, so these letters can be rearranged

explanation.surface: Discord in the music is, when all is said and done, just one option.
explanation.walkthrough: The commas make 'after all' look like an aside, but every letter of the phrase is part of the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a false relation is a chromatic clash between a note and its altered form in another part.

clue.text: With set expression, class cook cauli

parts.note: a form is a class in a British school

indicators.note: to cook is to doctor or falsify, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A school class follows a recipe to cook cauliflower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cook' shuffles CAULI into ULAIC. A form is a school class in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Formulaic means following a set formula or stock phrasing, so it is said with set expression.

clue.text: Plant put in a container like this

parts.note: taken as written
a can is a container
thus means in this way, like this

explanation.surface: Someone instructs how to pot a plant in a container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' could be a verb, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Acanthus is a Mediterranean plant whose leaves inspired Corinthian column decoration.

clue.text: Poor cases altogether for housing the homeless

definitions.text: Poor cases altogether for housing the homeless

parts.words: Poor cases altogether for housing the homeless
parts.note: poor cases are flimsy boxes; put all together they make a makeshift settlement where rough sleepers shelter

explanation.surface: A charity talks about destitute cases brought together for shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor cases' reads as needy people, but it also means flimsy packing boxes, which homeless people use as shelters.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names an area where homeless people sleep in boxes, as once at London's Bull Ring.

clue.text: Priest's assumption about the crown

parts.note: assumption here is putting something on, and the crown is the top of the head: what a cleric puts on over it

explanation.surface: A cleric makes an assumption regarding the monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assumption' reads as a guess, and 'crown' as the monarchy, but a priest assumes (puts on) a square cap over the crown of his head.
explanation.definitionFit: A biretta is the square cap worn by Roman Catholic clergy on top of the head.

clue.text: Have had to show such differences, serious

definitions.text: Have had to show such differences

explanation.surface: Variations seriously had to be shown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have' and 'had' differ grammatically: the present against the past form of a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Have and had differ in the grammatical sense of time; intense means serious or earnest.

clue.text: Feel sorry for river wader

parts.note: an egret is a wading bird like a heron

explanation.surface: Someone pities a wading bird by the river.
explanation.definitionFit: To regret something is to feel sorry for it.

clue.text: In new university, learnt to be unbiased

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone learned to be impartial at a newly founded university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' reshuffles U and LEARNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Neutral means taking no side, which is the same as being unbiased.

clue.text: Gorgeous type holding class needs a layer of protection

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a cutie is an attractive person
CL is the abbreviation for class

explanation.surface: An attractive person teaching a class needs some protection.
explanation.definitionFit: The cuticle is the protective outer layer of skin, especially at the base of a nail.

clue.text: No end of hard work I put in for part of church

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other
no end of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a chore is a tedious task, hard work

explanation.surface: A church volunteer puts in endless hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of' trims CHORE to CHOR, and 'put in' places I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The choir is the part of a church, beyond the nave, where the singers sit.

clue.text: Centre of planet getting hot at the start

indicators.note: at the start says the named letter is moved to the front of the word

parts.note: Earth is a planet
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: The core of a world is described as heating up first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting hot at the start' takes the H of EARTH and puts it at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart of something is its central or innermost part.

clue.text: Showing disappointment about place to die, wanting glory

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: sour describes someone looking disappointed or embittered
to end is to die or come to a close

explanation.surface: Someone bitterly let down about where they will die wants fame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to die' is a verb here, giving the verb for coming to a close rather than a place of death.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendour means magnificence or grandeur, which is glory in its sense of brilliant beauty.

clue.text: Sort of security for party

explanation.surface: Welfare benefits are linked to a gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Social security is state welfare; a social is an informal party or get-together.

clue.text: Western state seen in genuine high-performance car

parts.note: true means genuine

indicators.note: seen in means placed inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: GT, gran turismo, is a high-performance car
RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state

explanation.surface: A Western state is spotted in a real sports car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Western' looks like an adjective for the state, but it is the definition: a cowboy film.
explanation.definitionFit: True Grit is a cowboy film starring John Wayne, i.e. a Western.
